sections.text: ir.attachment keeps Odoo's metadata (name, parent record, type, URL, checksum, size, media type); the bytes live in a store that every node of a deployment shares (ADR 0041). A table never holds a file: it holds a reference to a blob addressed by its SHA-256, so identical files are stored once per database. You use the functions of erp_addon_base::attachments; you never write SQL and you never touch a path. Operators: the store and its settings are in [Attachment store for operators](/en/next/developer/installation/attachment-store.md).

base.attachment_max_bytes is the database-global administrator policy (ADR 0193). It is one value shared by declared Settings and Technical System Parameters: default 134217728 bytes, inclusive bounds 1–2147483647. Empty/absent resets to the declared default; invalid text refuses by name. Use the Settings service or the checked parameter API; never write either storage table directly. Technical edits advance the same Settings revision and audit as Settings edits. The attachment service enforces this policy on decoded bytes and server-owned staged/copy sizes; caller-supplied sizes cannot grant admission. The runtime file ceiling and inline threshold still apply. Larger content uses the native staged protocol; the browser's current base64 path remains bounded by the inline threshold. An upload-policy read does not grant generic parameter access. The attachment service rolls back consumed uploads on a size refusal; callers catching model-method errors must still use the ORM's outer savepoint contract (ADR 0014). Future HTTP uploads must use the same policy before reservation and during receiving. Administrators open Settings, choose the database scope, and edit **Maximum attachment size (bytes)** under Base. The same key appears in Technical → System Parameters; clearing its value resets it.

The API below, the ir.attachment model, the garbage collection jobs and the access rules of the generic ORM path are in this release. The signed-in download route is described under [Read a file in the browser](#content-route); bounded composer uploads use the thread RPCs in [Chatter storage](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/mail.md). The separate streaming-upload delivery is not complete. Not yet: binary fields stored as attachments (the BASE-B binary-field follow-up, needs a binary value in the ORM), the compiled parent-access rule that makes generic search follow the record (the BASE-B access follow-up), scanning, encryption and store migration (see the design note docs/design/m3-base-b.md section 1). Each fails with an error that names what adds it.

Content above the inline threshold (2 KiB by default) never passes through memory as a whole. A caller that holds the ORM (a route, a job's external step, a test) streams it into staging first: use erp_addon_base::attachments::{StageRequest, Uploader}; use erp_sdk::prelude::*; async fn stage( orm: &erp_sdk::Orm, env: &erp_sdk::Env, file: &mut (dyn tokio::io::AsyncRead + Send + Unpin), ) -> Result<()> { let staged = Uploader::new(orm) .stage(env, file, StageRequest::named("contract.pdf").declared("application/pdf")) .await?; // staged.id is bound to the subject and actor of env, expires in 24 hours and links once println!("{} bytes, sha1 {}, type {}", staged.size, staged.checksum, staged.mimetype); Ok(()) } The row that records the upload commits before the first byte is written, so a crash leaves a row that expires and a cleaner job removes the object; nothing ever lists the store to find leftovers. The type is detected from the first 8 KiB; a declared type that is not itself active (HTML, SVG, XML, script) on active content is refused naming both types. The intent also reserves its declared byte length, or the effective file limit when length is unknown. Use .with_declared_length(bytes) for a known length and .with_file_limit(bytes) for a transport limit; the configured attachment limit still caps both. Actual content cannot exceed its reservation, including content below the inline threshold. A shorter successful file reduces the reservation to its actual size. For this native staging API, that admission ceiling is the node runtime configuration. The database policy is rechecked when the staged file is adopted into an attachment. A lower database policy can therefore refuse adoption of an already staged file. The future HTTP route must also consult the database policy before reserving or receiving bytes; that transport is outside this slice. Pending count and bytes aggregate by subject across API keys and application nodes. Database staging bytes have a separate hard cap. An optional storage quota uses deduplicated committed content plus retained staging reservations. Direct inline writes participate in that quota and ledger too; copying an existing blob does not charge it again. Receiving has separate idle and absolute bounds: upload_idle_timeout_secs defaults to 30 seconds (1–300); upload_receive_timeout_secs defaults to 600 seconds (10–86400), capped by upload_ttl_secs. Only new body bytes reset the idle timer. Both inline probing and external staging use this reader. A transport may tighten these deadlines. Typed UploadIdleTimeout, UploadReceiveTimeout and UploadExpired sources distinguish their Validation errors. Failure/cancellation leaves a durable intent for fenced maintenance; it does not synchronously delete store objects. Its reservation remains until physical cleanup succeeds. An expired or consumed external upload can therefore still occupy the staging byte budget. Consumed uploads no longer occupy pending-upload slots; inline consumption releases its staging reservation. Adoption and its new-content charge roll back with the business transaction. An admitted upload is not admitted a second time when linked, regardless of whether it is inline or external; physical staging stays charged until cleanup. Storage-quota errors retain a typed erp_sdk::blob::BlobError::QuotaExceeded source; count refusal uses ResourceExhausted, and node admission uses Lock. Transport mapping belongs to the HTTP package. erp_sdk::Isolation is available to native composition code using BeginOptions::isolation; normal ORM business work keeps its default isolation. attachments::gc::compact_usage is an explicit bounded System maintenance primitive requiring READ COMMITTED. The fixed elevated base.attachment_usage_compact job schedules it through the isolated owner runner. Enable that node explicitly as described in the attachment-store operations guide.

use erp_addon_base::attachments::{self, AttachmentContent, NewAttachment, ParentRef, UploadId}; use erp_sdk::prelude::*; async fn attach(tx: &mut Transaction, partner: i64, upload: UploadId) -> Result<()> { let ids = attachments::create( tx, vec![ // a staged upload (any size) NewAttachment::new("contract.pdf", AttachmentContent::Upload(upload)) .on(ParentRef::new("res.partner", partner)), // bytes up to the inline threshold need no upload NewAttachment::new("note.txt", AttachmentContent::Bytes(b"hello".to_vec())) .on(ParentRef::new("res.partner", partner)), // a link to an external page (http or https) NewAttachment::new("site", AttachmentContent::Url("https://example.com".to_owned())), ], ) .await?; assert_eq!(ids.len(), 3); Ok(()) } create checks write access to every parent record once per model, links the content, and inserts the rows. Linking is one set-based step per batch: the upload is consumed (unexpired, same subject and actor, single use), the blob row of the digest is found or inserted (a unique key on the SHA-256, so two nodes storing the same bytes at once end with one blob and no race), and a blob that garbage collection had marked is revived only after its bytes are proved present. A rolled-back transaction leaves the upload usable again. create_unique is Odoo's: it reuses an attachment of the same content and type that the caller may write, else creates one.

A chatter composer uploads its files before the message, and so before the record that will own them, is known. Until the HTTP upload route exists, the mail addon's thread_upload RPC call (see [Mail](/en/next/developer/addon-guide/mail.md), base64 content up to the inline threshold) is that route: it stores them with NewAttachment::pending_in("mail.compose.message"): the row names the placeholder model, has no record id, and is standalone to the access rules (its creator and the system group see it). The post path then claims them with attachments::adopt, after it has checked the right to post on the record: use erp_addon_base::attachments::{self, AdoptScope, AttachmentContent, NewAttachment, ParentRef}; use erp_sdk::prelude::*; async fn composer_flow(tx: &mut Transaction, ticket: i64) -> Result<()> { // the upload route: the message does not exist yet let draft = attachments::create( tx, vec![ NewAttachment::new("quote.pdf", AttachmentContent::Bytes(b"%PDF".to_vec())) .pending_in("mail.compose.message"), ], ) .await?; // the post: after the caller's post access on the record was checked attachments::adopt( tx, &[draft[0].get()], ParentRef::new("helpdesk.ticket", ticket), &["mail.compose.message"], // an internal caller may also name files already on the record AdoptScope::ComposerAndRecord, ) .await?; Ok(()) } adopt accepts an id only if it is the caller's own file in one of the placeholder models, or, with AdoptScope::ComposerAndRecord, already on the record (not field-bound). AdoptScope::ComposerOnly is for a caller outside the internal group (the chatter passes it for a portal user, as Odoo keeps only their own composer files): a file already on the record is refused by name like any other. For the files already on the record ComposerAndRecord also requires write access to the record (Access otherwise), as Odoo's post route refuses a file the caller may not write. adopt is not for public or shared principals until scoped principal tokens exist: its creator test compares the caller's user id. Anything else, a missing id included, refuses the whole call with Access, names the ids, and moves nothing. The move is one set-based write as the system, because the right that matters is the right to post (a portal user may post on a record they may only read, and has no right on the file table); reattach is the call to use when the caller must hold write access to the target. A composer file that no post ever claims is removed by the staging cleaner job after attachments.composer_retention_secs (default 24 hours, at least one hour; CleanReport::abandoned); the cleaner only touches rows of the composer placeholder model with no record id.

use erp_addon_base::attachments::{self, ListOptions}; use erp_sdk::blob::ByteRange; use erp_sdk::prelude::*; async fn show(tx: &mut Transaction, partner: i64) -> Result<()> { // the chatter panel: what the caller may read of this record's files let files = attachments::for_record(tx, "res.partner", &[partner], ListOptions::default()).await?; for file in &files { let handle = attachments::open(tx, file.id).await?; // a range, streamed: nothing is loaded whole let first = ByteRange::new(0, 1024.min(handle.size()).max(1)); let part = handle.open(Some(first)).await?; drop(part); } Ok(()) } open returns a BlobHandle: size, type and checksum come from the database before any byte is fetched; open(range) streams; read_to_vec(max_bytes) refuses content above max_bytes up front and checks the SHA-256 of what it read. Missing content is an AttachmentContentMissing internal error, never an empty body (Odoo serves an empty file: ir_attachment.py:145-152).

The browser reads a file by attachment id at /erp/content/<id> (Odoo's /web/content/<id> is served in place, so existing links keep working). Our web client's chatter uses it for thumbnails and ?download=true for the download link. What the route does (SPEC-BASE-175): - it needs a signed-in browser session (401 without one; an Authorization header is 401 for now, bearer reads come later); only GET and HEAD (405 with Allow: GET, HEAD); - only internal users are served: a portal or public caller gets the 404 (SPEC-BASE-150; portal reads come with link principals). The read check is the one of "Who may see a file" below, run under the caller's principal in the session's transaction before anything else. No company selection is needed in the URL: a session reads with all of the user's allowed companies. A missing id, a refused read, a record of another company, a URL attachment and one without stored content all answer the same 404; - the transaction ends before any byte is read; one byte range is 206, several, malformed or unsatisfiable ranges are 416 naming the reason, and If-Range returns the whole file (there is no ETag yet); - query keys: download=true|false and mimetype=application/octet-stream; anything else is 400; - headers are the attachment class: Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, Cache-Control: private, Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin, an RFC 6266 Content-Disposition with filename*. Only PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and PDF are inline (and not with download=true); HTML, SVG, XML, JavaScript and WASM are served as application/octet-stream; - a node with every stream permit in use answers 503 with Retry-After: 1; content whose bytes are gone is 500 AttachmentContentMissing <request id> (the attachment and digest are in the server log). Native code reads the same way with attachments::content::lookup_content(tx, id): it takes the caller's transaction, does the check itself and returns ContentLookup::Found with a RouteContent that stays usable after the transaction ended (open(range) takes the stream permit and opens the bytes). There is no entry that returns bytes by id without the check. Not in this route yet: /web/image, model/id/field paths, access_token and public files, URL-attachment redirects.

use erp_addon_base::attachments::{self, ParentRef}; use erp_sdk::prelude::*; async fn move_files(tx: &mut Transaction, attachment: i64, message: i64) -> Result<()> { // an activity's files move to the message when it is done attachments::reattach(tx, &[attachment], Some(ParentRef::new("mail.message", message))).await?; // a copy references the same blob: no byte is copied attachments::copy(tx, &[attachment], Some(ParentRef::new("mail.message", message))).await?; Ok(()) } Deleting a record deletes its attachments, in one statement per unlink call: the composition root registers attachments::UNLINK_HOOK (the server composition does). Deleting an attachment removes the row only; the blob becomes a garbage candidate through a statement trigger, and the collection job removes its bytes after the grace period if nothing references it any more.

Access derives from the record the file is attached to (Odoo _compute_res_access): a record-bound attachment is allowed when the caller may read (write, for create, write and delete) the parent; a field-bound one needs access to that field too, except for the system group; a standalone one belongs to its creator and the system group; a parent that no longer exists, whose model is not installed, or that is security data is denied, and a missing attachment looks the same as a refused one. Checks are explicit and batched, one per parent model per call. Until the compiled parent-access rule lands, the generic ORM search and read of ir.attachment are limited: the system group sees everything, internal users see only the attachments they created, public and portal users see none. Use for_record and open for the record-derived view. Treat metadata visibility, file delivery and mutation as separate checks. A record reader can download a file uploaded by another user without being able to read that file's generic metadata row. Conversely, the creator's metadata grant does not authorize downloading or moving a file after it has been bound to a record the creator cannot access. Rebinding checks write access on both its current and proposed parent, including a changed res_field; a refused batch leaves the binding unchanged. The current /erp/content/<id> route requires a signed-in session even when the row has public=true. The public content capability of SPEC-BASE-143 is separate, unimplemented behavior; the flag grants no anonymous JSON-2 metadata access. Native multi-user acceptance for these distinctions is in crates/erp-cli/tests/multiuser_mail_attachments.rs (partial SPEC-HUMAN-033 coverage). The service checks the caller first (parent access and, for a binary attachment with a URL, which a copy keeps, the serving group), then writes the rows as superuser inside a private scope. An addon's override of ir.attachment create or write that runs during that write, and anything it calls in the same transaction, sees the superuser environment and inherits the scope: do its own checks from the values, not from the environment.

| Situation | Kind | Message starts with | |---|---|---| | Parent refused | Access | Sorry, you are not allowed to access this document. | | Upload unknown, expired, used or another user's | Validation | The upload is not usable: | | Storage quota or a database/subject staging-byte budget is exhausted | ResourceExhausted | This file cannot be uploaded because the attachment storage limit | | Subject pending-count cap is reached | ResourceExhausted | Too many uploads are pending. | | Receive outlives its durable intent | Validation | The upload intent expired | | Declared type does not match the content | Validation | declared content type | | Bytes above the inline threshold passed in memory | Validation | Content above | | No attachment runtime attached | UserError (422) | Attachments are not configured: | | Several nodes, node-local store | Programming | The attachment store | | Content missing from the store | Internal | AttachmentContentMissing: | | Every streaming permit of this node held (stream_permits_per_node, per node); retry shortly | Lock | every attachment stream of this node is in use | | Copy of a binary attachment with a URL, without the serving group | Validation | Sorry, you are not allowed to write on this document | | adopt of a file that is not the caller's pending file or (with ComposerAndRecord) already on the record, or that does not exist | Access | These attachments cannot be linked here: | | adopt of more than 1000 ids or a non-positive id | Validation | At most 1000 attachments are claimed / An attachment id is a positive number | | A pending file with a parent or a field | Validation | A pending attachment belongs to a placeholder model |

| Odoo | Here | |---|---| | attachment.raw, datas, db_datas, store_fname, index_content | none: bytes are blobs; use open and Uploader; text indexing is the M5 extraction task | | ir_attachment.location | server configuration attachments.write_store; writing the parameter is refused | | _filtered_access, check | the explicit parent check inside every function above | | create_unique | create_unique | | copy | copy: shares the blob | | file served empty when missing | an error | | XML and SVG neutered to text/plain for non-administrators | the detected type for everyone; active types are served only as downloads (HTTP route, planned) | | SHA-1 checksum as the file address | SHA-1 stays in checksum; the address is SHA-256 |

- Odoo's filestore is a directory on one node (ir_attachment.py:99-101, _filestore), so several application servers need a shared filesystem or an add-on; here the store is shared by design (an object store, or a shared path declared by the operator), and a node that mounts another directory refuses to serve. - Odoo collects garbage by marking files in a checklist directory on every write and walking it later (ir_attachment.py:161-162,224-242,265-371); here references are database rows guarded by a foreign key, unreferencing enqueues a candidate, and any node runs the collection as a leased job. - Odoo compares whole files to deduplicate because SHA-1 can collide (:164-170); here the key is the SHA-256 and the unique index decides. - Odoo filters attachments in Python and gives up past a candidate limit (:43-44,779-782); here the parent check is one batched call per model and there is no such ceiling in the API.

The planned POST /erp/attachments/upload route will return {upload_id, size, checksum, mimetype}. A native composition adapter will stream into Uploader; the HTTP crate will not depend on the base addon. Existing typed staging/linking APIs remain the implemented path. Chatter RPCs still use bounded base64; their planned upload_id alternative and thread_post staged descriptors must not be called until the HTTP/mail implementation is available.

erp_blob::AttachmentStore exposes owner, put_owner, check_owner, contested, create_contested and probe_owner. The memory store and object-store adapter implement these low-level operations. LocalStore implements them on Linux and macOS through exclusive-create leases, a stable OS advisory guard and atomic no-replace rename. Other platforms retain typed unsupported defaults. An advertised capability never grants ownership admission by itself. OwnerIdentity records the cluster identifier, database OID and database incarnation. OwnerMarker adds a positive generation, a unique operation UUID and Unix seconds. Its strict v1 encoding rejects extra bytes and unknown formats. OwnerVersion preserves the backend ETag and optional version identifier; keep both in durable coordinator state. Tokens reject wildcards, lists and header control characters. OwnerState pairs a record with the version from the same read. Passing no expected version to put_owner means create-only. Passing the last confirmed version means compare-and-swap; a failed precondition returns BlobError::OwnerConflict. The coordinator must persist its intended operation before issuing the put. An existing contested marker is never overwritten, and the store API has no operation to clear it. check_owner checks the current owner, not an old version selected by a versioned-object query; it does not also check contest absence. Run probe_owner against each configured backend before accepting its ownership capabilities. It exercises create-only writes, stale and matching conditional writes, current-owner checks and create-only contest writes in a fresh random namespace, then removes only its own probe markers. LocalStore exclusively creates the probe namespace before it can own cleanup; an existing namespace is refused intact. A probe failure is an error even when the advertised capability flag is true. Cleanup failures retain the original probe error and the cleanup error in OwnerProbeCleanup; failed probe objects may remain in that private namespace. No content or staging object is removed by the probe. These primitives do not activate maintenance. The coordinator API below adds heartbeat health and durable observation. Sweep and staging-cleanup primitives enforce current ownership; shared-filesystem peer admission and native runner activation remain pending. Native composition must complete those parts before admitting destructive maintenance. The clone isolation procedure in the operator guide remains required. The executable marker examples are in crates/erp-blob/tests/owner_contract.rs. Object-adapter coverage uses an in-memory object store; live S3-provider behavior remains unverified. Local process fixtures are in crates/erp-blob/tests/local_owner_process.rs and crates/erp-blob/tests/support/local_owner.rs. They establish local primitive behavior, not whole application/database or shared-filesystem admission. Local owner records pair the canonical marker with a fresh publication nonce. Persist the returned opaque version unchanged; publishing the same marker again still changes its version. A single open file yields the marker and token together. The implementation syncs temporary records before naming them and syncs the namespace directory before acknowledging publication. The local lease lasts 30 seconds and contains an acquisition nonce, advancement operation and expiry. A verified expired lease can be moved aside; changed lease data is restored with no-replace rename. The stable .owner.guard interlocks final validation, publication and release. A paused holder inside that guard causes retryable refusal, even after lease expiry. A resumed stale holder cannot publish or remove a successor's lease. Guard/lease contention is retryable Unavailable, distinct from OwnerConflict. Reads and writes of malformed state fail explicitly. A failure after publication can leave the intended owner installed. Recover by reading the exact persisted intended operation through the ownership coordinator; never assume an error undid the put. A truncated lease after a process crash refuses further advancement instead of guessing expiry. Recovery artifacts remain for diagnosis when safe restoration fails. No automatic force claim or manual marker-deletion procedure is provided by this library slice.

attachments::ownership implements ADR 0041's owner protocol as explicit transaction boundaries. An owner-side native consumer commits prepare(tx, store_key, Purpose::Heartbeat) in READ COMMITTED, performs Prepared::execute() outside the transaction, then commits settle(tx, &prepared, attempt). Only after that commit does it interpret Settlement. A retry retains the exact pending marker; a successful external write with a lost database commit is recovered by exact marker equality. A matching database identity or a larger generation alone is insufficient. ContestPending means refusal is durable before marker publication. The consumer publishes the create-only contest outside a transaction and commits settle_contest; a publication failure keeps the pending refusal and its typed storage error. Contests are never cleared automatically. HeartbeatJob provides that fenced native sequence. It is registered as base.attachment_owner_heartbeat and gc::ensure_schedules keeps its recurring row under the shared ownership::SINGLETON. Each beat prepares with Purpose::Observe, which opens a cleanup observation window when none is open and keeps an open one, so scheduled cleanup is admitted 660 seconds after the first healthy beat. Running it still needs an owner-role ORM and the privileged native-handler allowlist of ADR 0165 D5; the runtime role cannot write ownership state and fails loudly. gc::clean_staging and gc::sweep_mark admit each external store once per call. A store that is not admitted is left out (its rows, bytes and reservations stay), the refusal is logged at error level with the store and the reason, CleanReport::skipped counts the staging rows left, and CleanReport::refused / SweepMark::refused name each refused store (`RefusedStore { store_id, reason }; reason is the fixed text of the refusal, or store_error). sweep_mark` returns a SweepMark { ids, refused }; pass ids to sweep_remove. Inline rows and other stores are still cleaned. gc::check_cleanup returns the exact refusal for one store. Shared local stores are refused whatever the peer-probe evidence: no cleanup path reads it yet. The heartbeat handler persists {"after": <last visited store key>, "refused": {<key>: <code>}} in its job progress: a yielded run resumes after after, which is cleared only after a complete cycle. A store it cannot advance is recorded with an ownership::Refusal code and skipped, so the following stores are still beaten, and the run does not fail for it. health(&runtime_orm, store_key) and observation open a fresh primary READ COMMITTED transaction, close it before store I/O, and validate current store markers. No elevated connection enters these read APIs. Health expires after 600 seconds without a confirmed heartbeat. These APIs are not yet wired to all upload/link/revive call sites; FENCE integration retains that obligation. Starting Purpose::Observe establishes a durable 660-second window. Healthy heartbeats update the current owner version while preserving its anchor. Ambiguous recovery or a heartbeat gap invalidates continuity. Waiting returns a delay to reschedule, holding no transaction or connection. Ready returns a window identity, never permission to delete. The sweep and cleaner recheck owner/contest, identity, observation, holds, references and capabilities at each removal chunk. Shared local storage remains refused until maintenance integrates and verifies peer evidence. Borrowed-store sweeping remains unsupported. Complete SPEC-UPLOAD-010 and separate-process SPEC-BASE-158 acceptance remain pending.

erp_sdk::blob::peer separates actual local primitive observations (LocalPeer::step) and successful private cleanup (PeerCleanup) from raw transcript bytes. These private-field types have no public success constructor or deserializer. verify_transcript validates the fixed primitive transcript; it is not an authorization token. The native base API attachments::peer_probe stores one current attempt per store. Use owner-side primary READ COMMITTED transactions with an OperationIdentity for every audited transition; commit and drop each transaction before filesystem I/O or waiting. start, join, ready, record, finalize, fail and completed support the operator CLI. finalize consumes an actual cleanup proof and commits verified evidence with its typed audit event. The event retains the bounded node identifiers (one at start, both after join), so replacing the current row does not erase the audited pair. No API imports a success receipt. Runtime roles receive SELECT only on ir_blob_peer_probe. A future cleanup integration must call peer_probe::admit with the current node, automatically collected host provenance and current physical mount binding. It rechecks the fingerprint without the runtime's fingerprint cache and refuses an unlisted or changed participant. This is only the peer prerequisite: retain the ownership coordinator, contest, observation, hold, borrowed-store and per-chunk checks. The current scope is the verified pair; additional hosts need explicit admission. Operator usage, limits and remaining activation work are in the installation attachment-store page.

Storage promotion publishes content create-only and retains its staging source. A failed local receive may retain its deterministic .part file. Keep the committed upload intent until the cleaner removes both forms; callers never remove staging after a failed or successful link. External staging reservations remain charged until physical removal succeeds or absence is confirmed. This applies to deduplicated uploads too. Inline consumption releases its reservation transactionally; rollback restores the original ready intent and reservation. The native maintenance consumer establishes observation with the committed prepare/execute/settle sequence above and reschedules while waiting. It must keep the heartbeat healthy during the wait. It can check admission inside its actual owner-side READ COMMITTED transaction: use erp_addon_base::attachments::gc; use erp_sdk::{Result, Transaction}; async fn admitted(tx: &mut Transaction) -> Result<()> { gc::check_cleanup(tx, "main").await } This check holds coordinator/metadata locks until the transaction ends. It is neither a reusable permit nor a reason to sleep inside the transaction. sweep_mark, sweep_remove and clean_staging check again themselves. Their batch size is 1–1000. Both sweep transactions and staging cleanup use READ COMMITTED. Roll back on any error: partial external deletion can have happened, while database rollback retains the intent or sweep-attempt marker for an idempotent retry. BlobError::CleanupRefused names a fixed admission reason and remains the source of an Internal ORM error. Missing conditional or peer capabilities use OwnerCapabilityMissing; backend failures retain their typed cause. Multipart abort failures preserve the receive error and a separately redacted abort diagnostic in StagingAbort. Incomplete multipart sessions still require provider lifecycle cleanup after a crash. No listing-based recovery or automatic contest clearing is added. This library seam grants no SQL privileges and activates no schedules. A System principal on a request-role connection still cannot execute privileged cleanup. The maintenance composition must use its isolated authorized role; the general runner remains on its runtime role (ADR 0165 D5).

attachments::create_pending(tx, placeholder, limit, items) creates a batch that awaits a parent record. Check the caller's intended operation first. Items supply no parent, field or placeholder; the helper assigns the validated placeholder, derives the subject from the transaction principal, and admits against the actual pending rows. Limit and batch are bounded by MAX_BATCH (1000). An empty batch returns no ids. Invalid items or an exceeded cap create nothing. A full cap is a Validation error with PendingLimitExceeded as its typed source. A consumer may map that source to its own recovery message; it must propagate all other errors. A shared guard row prevents stale repeatable-read snapshots from over-admitting: PostgreSQL returns 40001 and normal whole-call retry obtains a fresh snapshot. Own flushed writes count. The helper's savepoint and guard share the business transaction; no independently committed reservation survives rollback. Do not perform body transfer inside this operation. Direct staged posts use ordinary batch creation and adoption in their one transaction, since no waiting file is committed.

attachments::recovery is an owner-side operator API (ADR 0183), never an RPC shortcut. inspect returns the validated database/store snapshot; begin commits a closed operator reason and audit before external effects. Its Claim::id is the durable resume identifier. resume reloads that same operation, Claim::phase reads progress, and Claim::run performs bounded resumable phases. The ORM must have the real attachment runtime attached to its registry generation and a ready audit store. Actual relation ownership is checked; a System environment alone does not authorize recovery. Store primitives are low-level ports and must not be called to bypass this audit path. An active recovery makes ordinary ownership health unavailable and refuses prepare/settlement. Errors retain their kind/source and identify incomplete operations. A successful claim invalidates old observation; it is not a deletion capability. The CLI runbook is in [Attachment store for operators](/en/next/developer/installation/attachment-store.md#audited-force-claim).

Quota admission reads at most attachments.usage_delta_read_limit deltas plus one overflow sentinel in one snapshot. Excess backlog and unknown legacy occupancy return typed AccountingUnavailable; quota/pending/timeout errors retain typed causes with safe public messages. The compactor folds only the actual DELETE RETURNING set. Its batch and interval are validated database parameters. gc::maintenance_kinds() is the fixed exact-declaration list for native server composition. Addon payloads, model methods and an arbitrary elevated declaration cannot join it. The owner ORM omits package hooks. Metadata GC/reconcile calls require maintenance authority and READ COMMITTED, like their scheduled handlers. External deletion remains separately fenced per store and chunk.

File bytes never live in a business table. Metadata, references and the garbage collection queue are in PostgreSQL; the bytes are in a store that **every node of the deployment reaches**: an S3-compatible bucket, or a local path that all nodes mount from shared storage (ADR 0041). A directory that only one node can see is a single-node setup and the deployment refuses to run a second node on it.

Stores are server configuration, never database data, and credentials never appear in it. [attachments] write_store = "main"            # where new content goes inline_max_bytes = 2048         # content up to this size is a database row (0 to 65536) max_file_bytes = 134217728      # one attachment, at most (1 MiB to 2 GiB; file_size is an Odoo integer) gc_grace_secs = 86400           # an unreferenced blob keeps its bytes this long (3600 to 30 days) stream_permits_per_node = 32    # streaming operations ONE node runs at once (1 to 1024); per node, not cluster-wide staging_max_bytes = 4294967296  # hard database staging reservations (default 4 GiB) upload_idle_timeout_secs = 30  # no new body bytes (1 to 300 seconds) upload_receive_timeout_secs = 600 # whole receive (10 to 86400), capped by upload_ttl_secs
[attachments.stores.main] kind = "s3" bucket = "erp-files" region = "eu-west-1" prefix = "tenant-acme"          # keys live under this prefix; one bucket may serve one operator

- **Credentials** for s3 come from the process environment (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN) or an instance role, never from this file. Give the application role read, write and delete on the prefix only; listing the bucket is needed only by the verification role. - An unknown key, an unknown kind, a value outside its bounds, a relative path, an endpoint that is plain http outside a loopback address, a missing write_store, encryption = "on" and a scan mode other than off fail at startup naming the setting. The postgres kind (small sites, bytes in the database) is not built yet (the BASE-B postgres-store follow-up). - **Hosting.** One bucket with a prefix per database is fine for one operator. A multi-tenant host must give each tenant its own bucket, or credentials scoped to its prefix. - Writing the Odoo parameter ir_attachment.location is refused: it names this configuration. The server (erp server --config server.toml) opens the stores with AttachmentConfig::from_toml and AttachmentRuntime::open (crate erp-blob) at start and attaches the product to every registry generation. **With no [attachments] table the server uses the default of ADR 0041 (lead ruling 3): a local store, id main, in the directory attachments next to server.toml.** The server creates the directory (mode 0700) when it starts, so an installation needs nothing else; the directory belongs to the user that runs the server and must be kept with the database in the backup. To place it elsewhere, or to use S3, write the table (it goes after the plain keys of the file): [attachments] write_store = "main" [attachments.stores.main] kind = "local" path = "/var/lib/erpforall/attachments" An invalid table, or a store that cannot be opened, stops the start with an error that names the setting. A host that composes the ORM without a runtime answers every attachment call with UserError (HTTP 422), Attachments are not configured: ... set attachments.write_store .... What size a browser upload may have is a separate limit. Until the HTTP upload route exists, the chatter uploads through the thread_upload RPC call, which holds the content to attachments.inline_max_bytes (2 KiB by default, at most 64 KiB; set it in the same table). The database administrator can further restrict files using base.attachment_max_bytes, visible in Settings and Technical System Parameters. Default: 134217728 bytes; floor: 1; hard bound: 2147483647. Changes take effect on subsequent requests without restart. This value does not enlarge the inline path or override the existing node attachments.max_file_bytes ceiling. Administrators choose the database scope in Settings and edit **Maximum attachment size (bytes)** under Base, or edit the same key in Technical → System Parameters. Clearing the Technical value restores the default. All serving nodes must retain consistent node ceilings; bootstrap reports the current node's effective inline-path limit. limits.rpc_body_bytes stays node configuration because request buffering must be bounded before database policy is available. It counts the JSON envelope and base64 encoding, not just decoded file bytes. Stream permits, deadlines, staging reservations and storage quotas remain independent resource controls. Lowering the upload policy does not remove or block reading existing attachments.

There is no node-local authority: any node links, reads and collects, and losing a node loses no file. Configure the same quota, staging, pending-count and file limits on every serving node. Drain old writers and restart all nodes together when changing these installation limits; mixed configuration generations are not a supported limit rollout. How a misconfiguration is detected: - **Node registry.** More than one live node (erp_node, ADR 0057) while a local store lacks shared_filesystem = true makes uploads and the attachment schedules fail with The attachment store <id> is a node-local directory but N nodes are live .... The flag is the operator's statement that the path is shared storage; it is not probed. - **Store identity.** Each store has a random id (.store-id in the directory, a marker object in the bucket); the database records it the first time the store is used. A node that mounts another directory or another prefix finds a different id and refuses to read or write (not retryable), so files cannot silently split across two disks even if the flag was set wrongly.

Five job kinds run on the durable queue (see [Background jobs](/en/next/developer/installation/background-jobs.md)); there is no scheduler process and no leader, any worker may claim them, and each has a singleton key so one runs at a time per database: | Kind | What it does | |---|---| | base.attachment_gc | Phase A: marks blobs nobody references deleting. Phase B: after the grace, removes the rows and the bytes in chunks of at most 1,000 keys. | | base.attachment_clean_staging | Removes consumed uploads and expired ones with their staged objects; adopts the digest of an expired upload so a key promoted by a rolled-back transaction is removed too. | | base.attachment_reconcile | Walks the blob table by id and queues unreferenced blobs the statement triggers missed (a restore with triggers disabled). | | base.attachment_owner_heartbeat | Every five minutes: advances this database's owner marker in each configured store and opens the 660-second observation window when none is open. Without it no store-backed cleanup is admitted. It writes ownership state, so it needs the owner-role maintenance runner. | | base.attachment_verify | On demand (payload {"deep": true} re-hashes the bytes): reports missing, short or corrupt blobs; fails the job listing up to 20; repairs nothing. | **A blob another node is still writing is never deleted.** A writer holds a shared lock on the blob row from the link until its commit; the sweep locks rows exclusively and skips locked ones, so it never waits for or removes content a transaction is linking. A blob nobody references is first only marked; its bytes leave after gc_grace_secs and only if, in a second transaction, the row is still unreferenced and unlocked. A writer that arrives in between revives the row, after proving its bytes are present. The upload record is the write-ahead marker: it commits before the first byte reaches the store and is removed only after an admitted cleaner has removed its staging object. Link commit or expiry makes it eligible; neither proves that storage disappeared. A key removed whose transaction did not commit is simply reported absent the next time. **The schedules exist after every base install and upgrade.** erp db init and erp module install|upgrade with base in the operation create the recurring row of base.attachment_gc, base.attachment_clean_staging and base.attachment_reconcile when that kind has no live row (any state but dead), in the operation's own transaction. A row that exists keeps its next run time, a running row is left alone, and a dead letter gets a fresh row next to it. **Every erp server start does the same** before the node reports ready, on the owner connection and without the store topology check (that check stays at upload and before every destructive store call). Two nodes starting together should end with one row per kind: the creation runs under an advisory lock (expected from the code, not tested). A start that cannot keep the schedules stops with a short cause and does not serve. erp_addon_base::attachments::gc::ensure_schedules(&orm) does the same in its own transaction after the store topology check, and is idempotent across nodes. **Rows are not runs.** The rows run only where a job runner claims them. The isolated maintenance runner for these kinds (ADR 0165 D5) is planned; until it is deployed, nothing collects, cleans or reconciles on its own. Do not treat the presence of the rows as attachment maintenance being operational. **With the in-app runner on** (jobs_run_in_app = true), that runner leaves these rows alone: it excludes the elevated attachment kinds (base.attachment_gc, base.attachment_clean_staging, base.attachment_reconcile, base.attachment_verify; ADR 0165 D5, ADR 0185), so the rows stay ready, are never claimed and nothing goes dead. Running them is planned work. **A base upgrade during a server start.** erp module upgrade base while a node is starting can abort on a serialization error when both create the schedule rows at the same moment. Nothing is committed; run the upgrade again. **Old attachment dead letters.** A dead attachment schedule row (from an earlier release or a test) is not live, so the next start creates a fresh row next to it. Discard such dead letters rather than requeue them: a requeue collides with the fresh row on the queue's dedup index and is refused.

A backup that copies the store apart from the database must keep the sweep from removing files it has not copied yet. gc::hold(tx, seconds, reason) writes a durable row; the sweep removes nothing while any hold is unexpired. The tool renews it while it runs and checks at the end that it never lapsed; gc::release_hold ends it. Holds and the sweep are serialized by one transaction advisory lock (gc::GC_HOLD_LOCK). Both sweep transactions take it shared before they read the holds and keep it until they commit; hold takes it exclusive before it writes its row, so it **waits for every sweep that is already running** (one that read the holds before the new row existed) to commit. When hold returns and its transaction commits, no sweep that missed the hold is still removing keys, and every later sweep sees it. Start the backup's database snapshot only after the hold has committed. A hold may therefore take as long as one sweep chunk (at most 1,000 key removals) to return. The sweep refuses to run outside READ COMMITTED (its job kinds use it): an older snapshot could miss a hold it waited for.

- A file is streamed in 64 KiB reads; an s3 upload holds one 8 MiB part; a local upload holds the read buffer. No whole file is buffered by the store, and proving a stored file's digest (a revive after a sweep started, deep verification) streams it the same way. - **Required for s3: a bucket lifecycle rule that aborts incomplete multipart uploads** (for example after one day) on the prefix. An upload whose request is dropped mid-stream never sends the abort, and its parts stay billed and invisible to the cleaner, which only sees completed staging objects. Configure the provider's incomplete-multipart lifecycle rule before using that backend; a durable intent alone does not identify an interrupted provider multipart session. - At most 100 pending uploads per subject (pending_uploads_per_subject, configurable from 1 to 100); separate API keys share this allowance. Previously accepted values above 100 now fail startup. An upload expires after 24 hours, but expiry alone does not release its storage reservation. Consumed rows do not occupy a pending slot; failed zero-byte rows still do until cleanup succeeds. - attachments.staging_max_bytes always caps database staging reservations (default 4 GiB, configurable from 1 MiB through 9223372036854775807 bytes). Each subject additionally holds at most four times the applicable file limit in reservations. These byte limits are hard across nodes. - Optional attachments.quota_bytes declares a soft storage quota (at least 1 MiB, at most 9223372036854775807 bytes). Omit it for no storage quota; staging limits still apply. Usage includes distinct committed content and retained external staging reservations. Inline linking clears its reservation in the same transaction; external staging stays reserved until admitted physical cleanup. Deduplicated committed content is charged once, independently of retained staging. - Quota observations use a transaction snapshot and an insert-only ledger. Concurrent new-content transactions can overshoot the soft quota by their admitted content sizes, bounded by the number of concurrent operations times their applicable file/batch bounds. Use this bound when sizing storage. Hard staging admission remains serialized in short database transactions. - Failed receives retain their intent and reservation for fenced cleanup. Watch cleanup-pending ir_blob_upload rows (state 3), including cleanup_error. No active maintenance worker means these reservations may continue refusing admission; raising limits does not repair failed cleanup. - Upload reads stop after upload_idle_timeout_secs without bytes, and after upload_receive_timeout_secs total even with continuous progress. The total deadline never exceeds intent lifetime. Timeouts release the node stream permit, retaining the cleanup marker. - Quota reads refuse admission when more than 10000 usage deltas remain. Run the admitted owner compactor; do not delete ledger rows manually. Compaction folds the actual deleted deltas into the base in one transaction. The isolated owner worker schedules compaction when explicitly enabled. - Quota schema version 3 migrates under the lifecycle writer drain once; repeated addon sync validates columns, constraints, capture functions and triggers instead of recreating them. Unknown-size legacy uploads become state 3 with reservation_unknown=true and numeric reservation zero. This is unknown occupancy, not an empty-object claim. While one such row exists, every staged upload is refused ("temporarily unavailable"), and so is every new inline attachment content when quota_bytes is configured; with no quota, inline attachments are still created. Only the staging cleaner (base.attachment_clean_staging) removes these rows, and only once the store is admitted: set attachment_maintenance_run_in_app = true on a node and let the owner heartbeat complete its observation window. Count them before activation with SELECT count(*) FROM ir_blob_upload WHERE reservation_unknown. Never clear the flag manually to restore admission. Validate the migration on the deployment clone before activation and retain a recovery backup. - Watch, too: callers answered every attachment stream of this node is in use (409, retry). That node's stream_permits_per_node are all held; add nodes or raise the value (see below). - Watch: jobs of kind base.attachment_* in erp_job (dead letters), rows of ir_blob in state deleting that stay (a store outage), ir_blob_upload rows older than a day, and the size of ir_blob_gc_candidate (it should drain). - Not yet: malware scanning, encryption at rest, online migration between stores, the Odoo filestore import, database duplication that shares blobs, and automatic owner-fenced maintenance for a *clone* of a database sharing one prefix (see [below](#clones)).

| Limit | Scope | How it is enforced | Setting | |---|---|---|---| | One run at a time of each attachment job kind | whole cluster | the job queue's singleton key and lease, in PostgreSQL | none | | A hold stops every sweep, and waits for a sweep already running | whole cluster | a PostgreSQL transaction advisory lock (gc::GC_HOLD_LOCK) | none | | The sweep never removes content another node is linking | whole cluster | PostgreSQL row locks and the grace | gc_grace_secs | | Pending uploads per subject | whole cluster, hard | committed intent plus short ordered advisory locks and fresh READ COMMITTED reads | pending_uploads_per_subject (1–100) | | Staging bytes | whole database and subject, hard | durable reservations retained through failed cleanup, expiry and consumption | staging_max_bytes; subject allowance is four times the applicable file limit | | Storage quota | whole database, soft | compacted base plus visible insert-only deltas in one snapshot | optional quota_bytes | | Concurrent streaming operations: upload staging, proving a stored file, deep verification | **each node** | an in-process bound; a full node answers busy at once (409), it never queues | stream_permits_per_node (default 32) | The streaming bound is per node: the deployment's capacity is nodes × stream_permits_per_node, so adding a node adds capacity. It is not a cluster-wide cap; a cap on the total requests a bucket receives (an S3 account limit) is not built yet, so size the per-node value with the node count in mind.

A database restored next to its source (a staging copy, a clone for a test, a point-in-time restore) holds the same ir_blob_store row: the same store namespace and the same store id. If it is started with the source's [attachments] configuration, it opens the **same directory or bucket prefix**, finds the same .store-id, and passes every identity check. Its garbage collection then decides from *its own* references: content the source attached after the copy was taken is unreferenced in the copy. An unfenced worker could remove the source's keys. The sweep and staging-cleanup library entry points now require current ownership admission; automatic server composition remains pending. This does not remove ADR 0041's stopped-owner residual or replace clone isolation. Neutralise every copy **before any node or worker of it starts**: 1. Leave the source running; start nothing on the copy. 2. Copy the source's store to a location of the copy's own, **including the identity marker**: for local, copy the directory with its .store-id file (for example rsync -a /srv/erp/attachments/ /srv/erp-copy/attachments/); for s3, copy every object under the prefix, the .store-id object included, to a new prefix or bucket (for example aws s3 sync s3://erp-files/tenant-acme/ s3://erp-files/tenant-acme-copy/). Files the source added after the database copy was taken are harmless extras in the copy; files the source removed meanwhile are missing there (base.attachment_verify reports them). 3. Point the copy's configuration at the new location (path, or prefix/bucket) and give its credentials no access to the source's prefix. 4. Start the copy. Its sweep now removes keys only in its own location. If the copy does not need the files, point it at a new empty location instead: the store identity check then refuses every attachment read and write there (the store id differs), which fails loudly and removes nothing. **Prerequisite for the server wiring.** The work that wires AttachmentRuntime into the server must compose the owner fence of ADR 0041 decision 5 with an isolated maintenance runner. The delivered library checks <ns>/_owner, _contested, database identity, the observation window and capabilities in both sweep transactions and before staging removal. Server activation and real shared-filesystem peer admission remain prerequisites. Keep the clone procedure above.

Streaming HTTP upload and automatic maintenance are planned; this documentation update does not activate a route or job. Before activation the implementation must compose the delivered quota reservations and hard staging caps with the complete ADR 0041 owner fence, and a separate allowlisted attachment maintenance runner. Do not widen runtime-role grants or move the general job runner onto the owner connection to work around missing maintenance. The existing clone procedure and capability limitations above still apply. The object-store adapter now has low-level owner/CAS/contest marker operations and an explicit conditional-semantics probe. The in-memory test store implements the same operations. This does not protect scheduled cleanup by itself. The coordinator API below is delivered, but native activation remains pending. Library deletion enforcement is delivered; the clone isolation procedure above and ADR 0041's documented residual still apply. LocalStore now supplies the low-level marker protocol on Linux and macOS. Its capability probe exercises create/CAS, no-replace rename and advisory-guard exclusion on the local filesystem. Unsupported atomic operations refuse explicitly; a capability flag alone is insufficient. The shared-filesystem flag is still not peer-probe evidence. Before future destructive activation, two-node evidence must establish both exclusive creation and the guard's cross-node exclusion on the actual filesystem. No configuration key or CLI switch enables these planned protections in this delivery. Local owner markers are <namespace>/_owner and _contested. The implementation uses a 30-second .owner.lock lease and a stable .owner.guard. Keep the guard file in place: replacing or deleting it while a process is using the namespace can split its interlock. Internal guard files are private (mode at most 0600); owner/lease records are created with mode at most 0440 inside private directories. The store directory and namespace must not be symlinks for owner operations. A busy guard or live lease returns retryable unavailable. A verified expired lease is recovered without overwriting another holder. Missing OS support, malformed records, failed directory sync and failed restoration refuse advancement. A crash during initial lease creation can leave an incomplete lease; this delivery refuses it and provides no automatic repair command. Preserve artifacts and keep destructive maintenance disabled pending supported operator recovery. A put error after naming the owner can be ambiguous, so coordinator recovery must inspect the intended operation rather than retrying with invented ownership. Process-crash tests do not establish physical power-loss behavior on every filesystem. Application jobs disabled means an admitted maintenance worker is required; a recurring schedule row alone is not evidence of running cleanup. Upload HTTP remains a separate delivery. The isolated attachment worker below is explicitly enabled per node; ordinary application jobs can remain disabled. Upgrade base with the authorized owner-side lifecycle before publishing runtime grants. Drain old application writers for the schema/backfill transaction. The upgrade backfills existing distinct blobs and retained uploads once; legacy receiving rows without a size reserve the historical maximum file size conservatively until cleanup. An over-cap database remains readable but refuses new admission. Contract version 7 publishes append-only accounting and restricted attachment writes; older publishers must not be restored over it. Ordinary requests cannot delete tracking/content rows or compact usage. Schema synchronization and a focused upgrade fixture establish the additive path; server maintenance activation still belongs to its separate delivery.

The durable coordinator uses additive ir_blob_owner_identity and ir_blob_owner_state tables. An authorized base upgrade installs them without changing existing blobs, uploads or accounting and without inventing a heartbeat. Request roles get SELECT only; publisher contract v9 refuses missing ownership tables or effective write privileges through PUBLIC/inherited roles. Automatic restoration of an older publisher is refused because it could regrant writes to retained coordination state. The native heartbeat is registered as base.attachment_owner_heartbeat and scheduled by the same ensure_schedules call as the other attachment jobs; the served binary does not call it yet. Server maintenance composition, request write-health enforcement and shared-filesystem peer admission remain integration work. Sweep and staging deletion now enforce the coordinator's current admission state in the actual cleanup transaction. Existing configured storage is not proof that maintenance is operational. Do not clear store markers by hand as a substitute for an audited operator claim. Once integrated, a heartbeat advances ownership every five minutes and 600 seconds without confirmed success makes established ownership unavailable. Failed store writes do not refresh that timestamp. Each advancement persists its exact intended marker before the conditional write; restart recovers only that marker. A lost conditional claim records contest-pending before publishing create-only _contested; failed publication preserves refusal. Repeated upgrades and restarts never reset ownership identity. Cleanup observation is durable for 660 seconds (two heartbeat intervals plus a one-minute margin). Healthy heartbeat successors preserve the original window; uncertainty or a health gap restarts it. A live clone sharing an identity can contest during this interval. ADR 0041's residual remains when the original database is stopped or cannot reach storage throughout the interval: neutralize or rebase clones before starting jobs. The local primitives merged separately; real provider/peer proof remains an admission requirement; coordinator readiness alone never permits deletion.

erp attachments probe-store --peer verifies the filesystem primitives used by local owner fencing. Run it as an operator on **two distinct hosts** using their protected server configurations, different node_name values, the same tenant database and the same registered local store. Each configuration must declare shared_filesystem = true. The store must already be registered by the attachment runtime; the probe does not install or upgrade the database. Upgrade base and publish the current runtime grants before using the command. The audit store must be ready. On the first host: erp attachments probe-store --peer --config /etc/erp/server.toml --store main start --timeout 120 The process prints a fresh session UUID and waits. On the second host, before the deadline: erp attachments probe-store --peer --config /etc/erp/server.toml --store main join SESSION_UUID Inspect the current result with: erp attachments probe-store --peer --config /etc/erp/server.toml --store main status The timeout accepts 30–300 seconds. Both processes must finish successfully. The protocol checks fresh challenge visibility, exclusive creation, advisory-guard exclusion in both directions, conditional owner publication and no-replace preservation inside a new private probe namespace. It removes only that attempt's known artifacts and audits the result. It does not touch the real namespace's ownership or contested markers, content or staged uploads. Evidence is bound to the database incarnation, store namespace/fingerprint, protocol and the two node/host/mount bindings. Starting another attempt invalidates previous admission. Missing, expired, failed, incomplete or mismatched evidence refuses destructive admission. A pair does not certify additional hosts. Rerun after mount, storage, configuration or topology changes, including changes an OS mount/root identity cannot detect. Host provenance assumes trusted operators; it is not remote attestation against a privileged host administrator. On cancellation or failure, preserve unexpected private artifacts for diagnosis and start a fresh attempt after resolving the reported error. A cleanup or audit failure never publishes successful new evidence. A kernel filesystem call blocked by an unavailable mount may outlast the orchestration deadline. Do not replace or remove a real .owner.guard or _contested marker to force progress. Audited claim --force recovery is planned. The probe and pair-scoped admission API are delivered by PROBE, but no cleanup path reads the evidence yet: a verified probe admits no deletion today. Destructive-path integration and maintenance activation remain with CLEANUP/INTEGRATE and MAINTENANCE. Probe success alone does not satisfy owner, contest, observation-delay, hold or per-chunk checks. Same-host process fixtures do not certify an actual shared mount; this delivery has no actual two-host shared-mount certificate.

An admitted cleanup transaction locks the ownership coordinator, store metadata and owner rows, then the hold lock and content/upload rows. It checks the current store owner version and contest once per store for each chunk (staging cleanup and sweep marking), and again before each store's batch removal in the sweep. Uninitialized, recovering, stale or contested ownership refuses deletion; missing conditional capabilities refuse too. The 660-second observation wait happens between jobs, with no open cleanup transaction. Healthy heartbeats must continue throughout that wait. The scheduled heartbeat opens the window itself; on a new database store-backed cleanup starts about eleven minutes after the first healthy heartbeat, with no operator step. **A refused store is skipped, never silent.** When a store is not admitted (not yet observed long enough, owned or contested by another database, missing capabilities, unreachable), staging cleanup and sweep marking leave that store's rows, bytes and reservations in place and still clean inline rows and the rows of admitted stores. Each refusal is logged at error level on target erp::attachments with the store id and the reason ("attachment cleanup is not admitted for this store"), and the staging cleaner counts the rows it left in skipped in its job progress. A store that stays refused keeps its consumed staging reserved, so its uploads eventually fail with QuotaExceeded: treat a repeated refusal as an alert. **Which store, why and since when.** The progress of base.attachment_gc and base.attachment_clean_staging (the jobs admin screen, or erp_job.progress) carries "refused": {"<store id>": {"reason": "...", "since": <epoch seconds>}}. The reason is a fixed text (ownership is not admitted, observation is incomplete, namespace is contested, store binding changed, database identity changed, and so on) or store_error when the store itself failed (its error is only in the log). since is the database time of the first refusal of an unbroken run of refusals; a store leaves the list as soon as cleanup admits it again. A store with no due rows, or a run skipped by an active hold, is not checked and so is not listed. **A long refusal fails the run.** Once a store has been refused for longer than the 660-second observation period, the job first commits what it could clean, then fails for retry with code cleanup_refused and a message naming each store and its reason (last_error_code and last_error of the job). The job is retried, not dead-lettered. While the store stays refused the job retries at the queue's backoff cadence (jobs.backoff_base_secs, 10 seconds by default) instead of every 15 minutes, so expect extra short runs and repeated error lines until it is fixed. What to do: look up the store id in ir_blob_store, then act on the reason: - ownership is not admitted or observation is incomplete: check that the heartbeat runs (below); on a new database the first eleven minutes are expected, a few retries may show then; - namespace is contested or database identity changed: another database (often a restored copy) uses the same store prefix; see "Restored copies and clones" above and "Audited operator recovery" below; - store binding changed or store_error: compare the store configuration with ir_blob_store and check that the store is reachable. **The heartbeat continues past a refused store.** A store the heartbeat cannot advance (an active operator recovery, a contest, a changed store binding, a superseded operation or a failing store) is logged at error level on erp::attachments with its key and a fixed code, and the heartbeat moves on to the next store, so one store never leaves the others without heartbeats. Its run still succeeds and reschedules after five minutes. Its progress shows {"after": null, "refused": {"<store key>": "<code>"}} for the last completed cycle; the codes are recovery_active, contested, binding_changed, contest_pending, superseded, store_failed and store_invalid (the store has no fingerprint, its recorded owner marker is unreadable, or its owner generation is exhausted: repair the store or its configuration). After a cycle with no refused store the progress is null. A refused store's own cleanup stays refused (its heartbeat is stale), which the cleanup jobs report as above. A database error fails the heartbeat run and it is retried. A changed database identity, a configuration error or an unreadable progress value is permanent: the heartbeat row is dead-lettered (state dead, with the cause in last_error) and nothing beats until the next erp server start, which schedules a fresh heartbeat row. Fix the cause first. The same holds for the cleanup jobs when their stored refused progress is unreadable. **Known limit: one failed beat can start a cleanup_refused episode.** A single failed or refused heartbeat of a store (for example one store timeout) makes that store stale, and a fresh observation window has to complete before cleanup admits it again: up to about 960 seconds (one heartbeat interval plus the 660-second window). Because the failure threshold is the 660-second observation period, the cleanup jobs can report cleanup_refused for that store during part of this time and retry at the backoff cadence. This is expected; act only when it persists past the window. Shared local stores currently refuse destructive admission with an error saying that peer probe evidence is not read yet, including when shared_filesystem=true and including after a verified peer probe: cleanup does not read peer evidence yet, so a recorded probe admits nothing and the cleaners skip such a store as above. Reading the probe evidence in cleanup is a separate task. Neither the flag nor single-node local process tests establish two-node evidence. Borrowed namespaces remain explicitly unsupported for cleanup and their external objects are never removed. Promotion retains staging until maintenance. Local receive failures can retain .part files under the upload's deterministic path. Do not remove those files or their ir_blob_upload rows manually. A failed delete retains accounting/tracking; retry tolerates objects already removed before a lost reply or database rollback. A consumed external upload retains its byte reservation, but no longer occupies a pending-upload slot. Inline consumption releases its staging reservation in its business transaction. A consumed source retained as a local hard link is conservatively counted as logical staging occupancy, although the inode is shared. These are library protections, not evidence of an active owner runner. Before activating schedules, maintenance composition must supply its isolated authorized connection; the heartbeat schedule supplies the observation sequence. Runtime roles keep their existing DELETE/TRUNCATE and coordinator-write denial. Provider multipart lifecycle cleanup, peer probing, operator force claim and complete borrower support remain separate obligations. Actual proof and remaining limits are in the cleanup task report.

The MAIL upload package adds base infrastructure table ir_attachment_pending_guard. Upgrade base with the schema-owner connection before publishing request grants or starting this binary. The additive table has no seed data: pending creation registers a subject/placeholder pair on first use; a user deletion cascades its guard rows. Existing attachments need no count backfill. Request roles require SELECT and INSERT on this table, and UPDATE of generation only. They must have no DELETE, TRUNCATE, identity-column UPDATE, REFERENCES, TRIGGER or MAINTAIN rights. The grant publisher narrows those rights and startup checks effective grants, including inherited/PUBLIC rights. Publisher contract 10 adds attachment_pending: guarded-create; older contract restoration is refused before grant publication or release switching. Reconcile an older publisher explicitly; never regrant blanket writes to the retained table. This introduces no maintenance schedule. Mail RPCs accept ready staged ids while retaining bounded base64 input. HTTP staging and browser transport activation are separate packages; RPC support alone does not prove browser integration.

An active _contested record stops ownership advancement and cleanup. After identifying and isolating every competing database, select the database that must own the namespace. Use that database's protected server configuration and its owner connection: erp attachments inspect --config /etc/erp/server.toml --store main erp attachments claim --config /etc/erp/server.toml --store main --force \ --reason restore-primary --confirm '<exact Confirm token from inspect>' Inspection prints the selected database identity, namespace, observed owner and confirmation token. restore-primary and retire-clone are the supported reason codes. A changed snapshot requires another inspection. The command refuses a request-role connection, unavailable audit storage, changed store binding, copied physical database identity, malformed markers or generation overflow. The ownership coordinator must already be initialized; this command does not activate maintenance. A heartbeat advancement that is still in flight refuses the claim: the command reports that an advancement is in flight and asks you to let the heartbeat settle it. It is treated as in flight while it is younger than the jobs.job_deadline_secs catalogue hard bound on the database clock (an advancement dated in the future counts as young), or while a job of the attachment ownership singleton holds a live lease. After both have lapsed, for example when the store kept failing and the heartbeat stopped, the claim proceeds and its higher generation supersedes the stale advancement; completion clears it and the heartbeat continues above the claim's generation. Known limit: a heartbeat retry whose job lease lapsed (for example, a node that lost the database but still reaches the store) can keep writing until its admitted jobs.job_deadline_secs after its run started. An old pending marker does not record that admitted limit; lowering current policy cannot shorten the recovery wait, which conservatively uses the catalogue hard bound. If its owner write lands after the claim's decision but before the claim's own owner write, every resume of that claim reports that the ownership changed, and the claim cannot complete. No content is deleted and cleanup stays refused. Before you force a claim after a node failure, stop the failed node's server process (that ends its writes at once), or wait the deadline catalogue hard bound after the attachment ownership job last started. If a claim is already stuck this way, the fix is tracked separately; do not delete markers or recovery rows. The decision and its audit commit before storage mutation. Ownership is established by conditional write, then the exact observed contest is conditionally replaced with a resolution receipt. The receipt stays in storage as recovery evidence. A later conflict creates a new active contest; an old retry cannot erase it. Keep all writers sharing the namespace on the compatible protocol: drain and upgrade them before the first force claim. Upgrade base to version 1.13 to install the recovery tables. Contract v12 prevents an automatic rollback to a publisher that could expose the retained recovery state. Contract v13 grants exactly what v12 grants and only relabels the capability owner-write, progress-read (the owner connection writes claims, the runtime role reads progress); a restore between v12 and v13 is allowed in both directions. An incomplete command reports its operation UUID. Inspect the durable phase and resume that exact operation after correcting the reported failure: erp attachments status --config /etc/erp/server.toml --store main --operation '<UUID>' erp attachments claim --config /etc/erp/server.toml --store main --force --resume '<UUID>' Do not start a new claim to conceal an unknown commit outcome. Preserve _owner, _contested, .owner.guard, lease artifacts and database decisions. Manual marker deletion and malformed-lease repair are not supported recovery procedures. An inaccessible clone cannot be proven isolated by this command; making that operational decision is the operator's responsibility. Completion resets observation. Cleanup still needs a fresh 660-second observation window, current owner/contest checks and its normal hold/borrower/peer admission. Recovery removes no attachment content, staged upload, accounting reservation or legal hold. It creates no schedules or workers.

Set attachment_maintenance_run_in_app = true in the root of the private server TOML on nodes that should execute attachment maintenance. It defaults to false and is independent of jobs_run_in_app. This node setting determines execution topology before the owner pool opens. A disabled node reports that its schedule rows do not execute cleanup. At least one ready admitted node must run maintenance. The maintenance runner admits only the fixed native attachment handlers (including heartbeat and usage compaction). The ordinary runtime-role runner excludes elevated kinds. Both share process and database job slots; the owner ORM has no package/Wasm hooks and never enters an HTTP request. Its pool capacity is the configured jobs.workers_per_db plus one control connection. Across N maintenance nodes the connection capacity is N times that amount; actual active jobs retain the shared durable queue limits and live-node division. Readiness loss stops new claims; a generation change fences old owner transactions and supervision replaces the runner. Shutdown drains it within the server deadline. Request roles retain their DELETE/TRUNCATE/owner-state restrictions. The owner needs the blob, usage, ownership and job privileges; missing required privileges refuse maintenance startup. Keep credentials in protected external files. A scheduled heartbeat establishes the ownership observation window. External cleanup still requires fresh ownership, capabilities, applicable peer evidence and an absent contest on every destructive chunk. Borrowed/refused stores retain their bytes; safe inline cleanup can proceed. Metadata marking and reconcile require maintenance authority, READ COMMITTED and the hold/coordinator locks; they do not themselves authorize store deletion. The deployment clone migration and operator activation remain the designated lead's release steps, not a consequence of merging source. Technical policy is editable in **Technical → System Parameters**, with these defaults and bounds. Missing/empty values use defaults; malformed or out-of-range writes and reads fail by key. Existing TOML upload deadline values remain the fallback until an explicit database override is stored. | Parameter | Default | Allowed range | |---|---:|---:| | attachments.usage_delta_read_limit | 10000 rows | 1–10000 | | attachments.usage_compaction_batch | 1000 rows | 1–10000 | | attachments.usage_compaction_interval_secs | 30 seconds | 1–3600 | | attachments.upload_idle_timeout_secs | 30 seconds | 1–300 | | attachments.upload_receive_timeout_secs | 600 seconds | 10–86400 | | attachments.gc_interval_secs | 900 seconds | 1–86400 | | attachments.cleanup_interval_secs | 900 seconds | 1–86400 | | attachments.reconcile_interval_secs | 21600 seconds | 1–604800 | | attachments.maintenance_batch | 1000 rows | 1–1000 | | attachments.composer_retention_secs | 86400 seconds | 3600–31536000 | Interval changes apply at a handler's next run; existing due times are retained. An administrator may move a job row's due time using the ordinary job controls. No zero value means unlimited. Unknown legacy occupancy blocks new staging, and new inline content while a quota is configured, until fenced cleanup; a ledger backlog above the configured read window blocks soft-quota admission until scheduled compaction. Never delete ledger rows or clear recovery flags manually. The cleaner deletes a draft message's attachments older than attachments.composer_retention_secs, so set it above the longest time a user may spend writing one message.
